title: Missouri Paycheck Calculator 2026 – State and City Taxes
metaDescription: Estimate your Missouri take-home pay after federal taxes, Missouri income tax, Kansas City or St. Louis earnings taxes, Social Security and Medicare.
heading: Missouri Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Missouri paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Missouri income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable local earnings taxes.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your pay frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Missouri employees working or living in Kansas City and St. Louis may face additional municipal earnings taxes. These deductions can affect the take-home value of otherwise identical salaries.

Whether you work in Springfield, Columbia, Jefferson City, Kansas City or St. Louis, this calculator can help you understand your payroll deductions and manage your finances.

## How to Use the Missouri Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross earnings before taxes and choose your payment frequency.

Enter the federal and Missouri income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

If Kansas City or St. Louis earnings tax was withheld, enter the amount shown for the pay period.

Include retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other employee deductions. Use the full withholding amounts, including any extra tax withheld.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to understand your remaining net income.

For greater accuracy, use your latest payroll statement and Missouri Form MO W-4.

## Missouri Payroll Taxes in 2026

Missouri employees may encounter the following payroll deductions.

Not every Missouri employee pays municipal earnings tax. Your residence, employment location and applicable municipal rules determine whether these deductions apply.

## How Missouri State Income Tax Works

Missouri uses progressive income tax rates.

Its 2026 employer withholding formula applies the following annual payroll-period brackets after subtracting the applicable withholding deduction.

parts.caption: How Missouri State Income Tax Works

parts.markdown:
The highest rate applies only to the portion of adjusted earnings within that bracket.

Employers follow the official [2026 Missouri withholding tax formula](https://dor.mo.gov/forms/Withholding%20Formula_2026.pdf), rather than applying the highest rate directly to every dollar of gross income.

## Missouri Withholding Deductions

Missouri's 2026 employer formula recognizes the following annual deduction amounts.

parts.caption: Missouri Withholding Deductions
rows: Married and spouse does not work

parts.markdown:
These amounts reduce annualized taxable wages before the appropriate withholding rates are applied.

Married employees should pay particular attention to whether their spouse earns employment income. Using the larger deduction independently at both jobs could lead to insufficient withholding.

## Understanding Missouri Form MO W-4

Missouri employees generally complete Form MO W-4 to communicate their state withholding information to employers.

The form provides information about filing classification, spouse employment and additional withholding requests.

Federal Form W-4 is separate from Missouri withholding information.

Review your elections when starting employment, getting married or experiencing a significant change in household income.

Visit the [Missouri Department of Revenue withholding guidance](https://dor.mo.gov/taxation/business/registration/small-business/maintain/withholding.html) to learn more about employer calculations and withholding certificates.

## Kansas City Earnings Tax

Kansas City, Missouri, imposes a 1% earnings tax on qualifying earned income.

Residents are generally subject to the tax on earned income even when they work outside the city. Nonresidents generally pay it on qualifying earnings from work performed within city boundaries.

For example, an employee receiving $2,500 in wages fully subject to Kansas City earnings tax would have a local deduction of:

$2,500 × 1% = $25

The tax is separate from Missouri state income tax.

Employees working partly outside the city or working remotely may need additional income allocation calculations.

Read the official [Kansas City earnings tax guidance](https://www.kcmo.gov/city-hall/departments/finance/earnings-tax) to determine whether the tax applies.

Do not confuse Kansas City, Missouri, with Kansas City, Kansas.

## St. Louis Earnings Tax

The City of St. Louis also imposes a 1% earnings tax on qualifying employee compensation.

Employees living or working within the city may be affected by the tax, depending on the applicable residency and employment rules.

A paycheck containing $3,000 in wages fully subject to the tax would produce a $30 local deduction.

St. Louis also imposes a separate payroll expense tax of 0.5% on applicable employers.

This employer expense should not be treated as an ordinary employee paycheck deduction.

Visit the official [St. Louis employer withholding and payroll expense tax guidance](https://www.stlouis-mo.gov/government/departments/collector/earnings-tax/payroll-tax-info.cfm) for additional information.

## Missouri Income Tax Calculation Example

Consider a single employee earning $65,000 annually with 26 biweekly payments.

Annualized taxable wages:

$2,500 × 26 = $65,000

Subtract the applicable annual deduction:

$65,000 − $16,100 = $48,900

Apply the progressive withholding rates to the adjusted annual earnings.

The accumulated tax on the first $9,436 is $262.86.

The remaining adjusted earnings are:

$48,900 − $9,436 = $39,464

Tax on that portion:

$39,464 × 4.7% = $1,854.808

Annualized withholding:

$262.86 + $1,854.808 = $2,117.668

Biweekly withholding before applicable rounding:

$2,117.668 ÷ 26 = approximately $81.45

Employer withholding and reporting rounding procedures may affect the final amount shown on your pay stub.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Missouri Paychecks

Missouri employees remain subject to applicable federal income tax, Social Security and Medicare.

Federal income tax withholding depends on wages, filing status and Form W-4 information.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered earnings up to the 2026 annual wage ceiling of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers generally collect an additional 0.9% when Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for official federal payroll guidance.

## Missouri Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 6 = $225

Total gross earnings:

$1,225

If the entire amount is subject to a 1% municipal earnings tax, the local deduction would be $12.25.

Applicable federal and Missouri withholding would also apply.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about eligibility.

## Working Across Missouri State Borders

Missouri employees may live in Kansas, Illinois or another neighboring state while working within Missouri.

Interstate employment can create additional tax withholding and filing obligations.

Resident tax credits may help reduce double taxation, but employees should not assume that every neighboring state has a reciprocal wage income tax agreement with Missouri.

A standard single-state paycheck calculator may not capture all interstate employment circumstances.

Confirm applicable withholding requirements with your employer and the relevant state tax authorities.

## Managing Your Missouri Take-Home Income

Compare estimated net pay alongside housing expenses, transportation costs, healthcare premiums and employer retirement matching.

When evaluating jobs in Kansas City or St. Louis, consider the potential impact of municipal earnings taxes.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare different compensation arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Missouri's income tax rate in 2026?

Missouri's ordinary withholding schedule uses progressive rates up to 4.7%. Applicable deductions and withholding classifications determine the amount deducted from each paycheck.

### Do Kansas City and St. Louis have income taxes?

Both cities impose a 1% earnings tax on qualifying compensation. Residency, employment location and applicable municipal rules determine whether the tax applies.

### Does every Missouri employee pay local earnings tax?

No. Municipal earnings taxes depend on your applicable tax jurisdiction. Employees should not automatically apply Kansas City or St. Louis taxes to wages earned elsewhere.
